content: Lamivudine-HBV is a medication prescribed to treat hepatitis B infection. It is not a cure for hepatitis B and does not prevent the transmission of the virus to others. This medication is typically taken orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. To achieve the best results, it is important to take this medication regularly and at the same time each day to maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body. Do not stop taking this medication without consulting your doctor, as this may lead to worsening of your condition, reduced effectiveness of the treatment, or the development of drug-resistant strains of the virus. Common side effects of lamivudine-HBV include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, fatigue, and infections of the ear, nose, or throat. These side effects are generally mild and temporary. However, in rare cases, this medication has been associated with severe, potentially fatal liver problems and a buildup of lactic acid in the blood (lactic acidosis). These serious side effects are more likely to occur in women and obese patients. If you experience symptoms such as persistent nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or rapid breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Before starting lamivudine-HBV, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Additionally, this medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis), as these substances can exacerbate these effects. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. If you are using the liquid form of this medication and have diabetes, be aware that it contains sugar (sucrose), and you may need to monitor your blood sugar levels more closely. During pregnancy, lamivudine-HBV should only be used when clearly needed. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. This medication has not been shown to prevent the transmission of hepatitis B from mother to newborn. Additionally, lamivudine-HBV passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Lamivudine-HBV may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as liver function tests, potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctor that you are using this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To prevent the spread of hepatitis B to others, always use effective barrier methods, such as latex condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity. Regular medical and laboratory tests, such as liver function tests, blood chemistries, complete blood counts, and hepatitis B virus DNA levels, should be performed while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. Different brands of lamivudine-HBV may contain varying amounts of the active drug. Do not switch brands without consulting your doctor. If you have an HIV infection, you should be taking the higher-strength dosage of lamivudine. Properly store this medication as directed on the product package or by your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Discard this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
